title: CROW: Classifier-Routed Organization of LLM Wikis
abstract: LLM wikis have been proposed as an alternative to classical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): a large language model (LLM) incrementally organizes knowledge into a directory of notes that can be inspected directly and grows with little manual upkeep, at the price of LLM calls whose cost grows with the knowledge base. Many of these calls are spent on decisions rather than on writing: where a new source belongs, which notes it relates to, which notes answer a question. We introduce CROW (Classifier-Routed Organization of LLM Wikis), a decision layer for LLM wikis that delegates these routing and consolidation decisions to a general-purpose typed classifier, such as the recently released Jev, and reserves generative calls for the steps that require writing text. In CROW, ingestion relies on a short sequence of classifier calls and invokes an LLM only to summarize the incoming source, to name new folders and, when an existing note must be updated, to rewrite it, while retrieval uses the classifier to select the relevant notes and leaves to the LLM only the final answer. CROW does not replace the compilation of entity, concept and synthesis pages that gives LLM wikis much of their value. We specify how each decision maps onto classifier primitives, position the design with respect to memory systems for LLM agents, model routing and candidate-then-verify pipelines, and discuss the effects on cost and latency that we expect but have not yet measured, together with the main limitations.

title: Deterministic Idempotent Hamiltonian Energy and Boundary Fault Projections in Heterogeneous Seismic Elastodynamics and Strong-Motion Sensing
abstract: Predicting seismic ground motion, fault rupture progression, and elastic wave propagation across heterogeneous crustal formations is essential for earthquake early warning systems, structural hazard mitigation, and sub-surface geophysical imaging. Standard finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) discretizations of the first-order velocity-stress Navier–Cauchy elastodynamic equations often suffer from secular energy accumulation across high-contrast material interfaces, where numerical impedance mismatch causes unphysical energy growth over long integration horizons. In this paper, we formulate a deterministic Elastic Strain Energy and Fault Boundary Conservation Projector (Πelast) that enforces strict Hamiltonian energy preservation and Coulomb friction slip bounds on the discrete state manifold. By dynamically tracking external source work during tectonic rupture and retracting velocity-stress states onto the exact Hamiltonian energy level-set, the projector eliminates unphysical numerical energy explosion (84.52% in standard FDTD vs. 6.25 × 10-14% with projection) without altering local kinematics. We establish the algebraic idempotency (||Π2 - Π||∞ ≤ 10-14) as a structural property of orthogonal level-set retraction. Furthermore, we formulate an algebraic Legendre polynomial null-space sensor projector (Πsens) that eliminates quadratic baseline tilt from streaming strong-motion accelerograms with zero phase distortion and an execution latency of only 3.84 μs per sample. Evaluated on authentic USGS and JMA strong-motion records (1940 El Centro and 1995 Kobe), the framework enables stable physical displacement recovery and robust P-wave onset picking for automated regional earthquake alerting networks. title: The Semantic Bridge: A Blind Spot of Formal Verification
abstract: This preprint is about a limit of formal and mechanical verification. A proof assistant, a compiler, or a blockchain fork can confirm that a conclusion follows from a formal statement. What it cannot confirm is that the statement matches the real problem. The gap between a formalization and the problem it was meant to capture is what the paper calls the semantic bridge, and no mechanical checker closes it. The paper illustrates this in three settings: the formally verified Navier-Stokes result released in September 2026, smart-contract security, and a synthetic pharmaceutical worked example. In the Navier-Stokes case the proved statement and its public interpretation came apart, and the authors added a separate Comparator layer over Lean. The paper also cites the formal-methods literature, which already has a term for this failure (semantic hallucination) and has measured the gap between compilation and faithfulness. The anchoring discipline described in the paper is the operational core of the Refutation-Graded Rigor Taxonomy (REGRART; previously abbreviated RGRT, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21633998). The paper discloses the discipline and not the scoring calibration behind it. AI-assistance disclosure: the prose was drafted with the help of a large language model. The argument, examples, source selection, and technical claims are the author's own.

title: GraphRAG for Industrial Technical Documentation: A Controlled Evaluation and Component Ablation on Laser Manufacturing Manuals
abstract: We evaluate whether Graph-augmented Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) improves faithfulness over vector RAG for industrial technical documentation and which graph components drive performance. On a 512-page laser operator's manual (2,773 chunks, 883 questions), we conduct one-factor-at-a-time ablations of graph presence, vector-retrieval depth, and graph-traversal depth. Vector RAG achieves significantly higher faithfulness than GraphRAG (95.8% vs. 93.2%, χ²=7.01, p=0.0081), while graph context improves context relevancy (+4.7% at 1-hop), a faithfulness paradox. Removing edge expansion (0-hop) does not recover the gap (p=0.0004), implicating entity injection rather than relationship traversal. Evidence is consistent with LLM-extracted entity descriptions being abstractive paraphrases rather than verbatim spans, conflicting with faithfulness metrics requiring direct attribution. At 33.3% entity hit rate (1-hop), graph injection reduces faithfulness in this single-corpus, single-domain, single-model deployment. The primary levers are retrieval precision and grounding mode; generalization remains to be tested.

title: A BIO-Annotated Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Sorani (Central) Kurdish (V1)
abstract: This dataset provides a BIO-annotated Named Entity Recognition (NER) corpus for Sorani (Central) Kurdish, comprising 420,896 tokens across 26,365 sentences. Text was drawn from authentic Sorani-language sources, including sports news (yariga.net), general news articles (the KurdishTextCorpus, Hugging Face), and other publicly available Kurdish texts. To improve coverage of rare entity categories — including Blood Type, Military, and Telephone Number — synthetic examples were generated using large language models and subsequently reviewed and corrected by native Kurdish speakers for linguistic fluency and entity boundary accuracy. Each token is labeled using the BIO (Beginning-Inside-Outside) tagging scheme across 15 entity types, mapped to 31 unique BIO tags, spanning general categories (Person, Organization, Location) and domain-specific categories (Attack, Nationality, Military, Blood Type, Compound entities). Annotation was carried out by the authors together with two Kurdish linguists following written guidelines addressing entity boundaries, multi-word spans, and disambiguation of overlapping categories, reaching a Cohen's kappa of 0.86. The file contains three columns: Sentence (sentence identifier), Word (individual token), and Tag (BIO-format entity label). Each row corresponds to one token; consecutive rows sharing a Sentence identifier form a full sentence. This dataset supports the development and evaluation of NER models for Sorani Kurdish and other low-resource, morphologically rich languages. It accompanies the Data in Brief article "A BIO-Annotated Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Sorani (Central) Kurdish.

title: Near-optimal high-rate surgery from linear PCPPs
abstract: A central problem for surgery with quantum Low-Density Parity Check (LDPC) codes is the design of auxiliary systems which measure large sets of logical operators in parallel, while preserving sparsity and fault distance. We introduce a very general method for designing surgery gadgets which are 'high rate', meaning that the number of operators measured in parallel is large in comparison to the size of the auxiliary system. Given an arbitrary initial $[[ n, k, d ]]$ quantum LDPC Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code, and an arbitrary subcode of size $μ\leq n$ that contains $t \leq k$ logical qubits, the method produces a sparse high-rate surgery gadget with size $μ(\logμ)^{O(\log\log μ)}=μ^{1+o(1)}$ which measures all $t$ logicals in the subcode. The space overhead is asymptotically optimal up to subpolynomial factors, as the lower bound is $Ω(μ)$. This gadget is produced in time polynomial in $μ$. When logical measurement is performed using these surgery gadgets, the phenomenological fault distance is at least $d$ when performed for $d$ rounds. Our main result comes from relating surgery gadgets with relative cosystolic expansion to linear Probabilistically Checkable Proofs of Proximity (PCPPs), which allow a randomised verifier to probabilistically verify the input to a linear circuit, using only oracle access to the input and a claimed proof.

title: Decoupling Disease, Covariates, and Individual Variability: A Unified Disentanglement Framework for Medical Image Classification
abstract: Accurately isolating disease-related features from confounding covariates (e.g., age, gender, site) and individual variations remains a fundamental challenge in medical image classification. Traditional regression-based approaches may ignore non-linear relations between image features and true covariates. To overcome this issue, we present a generalized Medical Imaging Disentanglement Learning (MedIDL) framework. MedIDL maps image features into three mutually orthogonal latent spaces through specialized disentanglement heads: a disease classification head guided by a supervised loss, a covariate-alignment head constrained by cross-subject similarity matching, and a Gaussian head absorbing individual variations. We evaluated our framework across 7 datasets encompassing diverse imaging modalities. MedIDL outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised classification methods in accuracy across all datasets. Association analyses demonstrate that MedIDL successfully isolates target-specific latent representations. Gradient-based interpretability mappings localize pathognomonic patterns aligning with established clinical literature.

title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation
abstract: Generative world models offer controllable and repeatable closed-loop simulation for end-to-end and vision-language-action driving policies, but production deployment exposes three unresolved requirements: faithfully reproducing a mixed fisheye-pinhole rig at native resolutions; reconciling causal, per-timestep interaction with long-horizon stability and low latency; and preserving scene identity when a location is revisited. We present ZYT-World, a single architecture that natively generates four fisheye views with field of view > 180° and three pinhole views. Projection-specific Plucker adapters encode camera geometry, ego-motion adaptive layer normalization provides global motion control, and a lightweight pixel-aligned layout conditions traffic participants and signals through instance-level boxes, headings and colors. Heterogeneous training combines full-rig geometric coverage with high-resolution detail. Teacher forcing, causal consistency distillation, self-rollout distribution matching distillation, and RigCritic transform a 40-step bidirectional teacher into a one-step, per-latent streaming generator, with RigCritic evaluating the seven-view rig jointly. A 19M-parameter variational autoencoder decoder (TinyVAE), W8A8 quantization, and our inference engine reduce decoding, backbone, and incremental-execution costs, respectively. Finally, cross-trajectory pairs derived from real captures train a plug-in implicit-memory module that preserves place-specific evidence. On the internal multi-view test set, the one-step model retains more than 90% of the teacher's PSNR and SSIM, while FID, FVD, and LPIPS stay within 11% of the teacher. Under the generator-only timing in Figure 2, it is 107.7 times faster than the 40-step bidirectional teacher. TinyVAE decodes 59.8 times faster than Wan. 30s rollouts and cross-trajectory revisits show the intended long-horizon and memory behavior.

title: The Silk Blanket Paradox — Evidence Review 2026
abstract: The Silk Blanket Paradox — Evidence Review 2026 examines the evolution of the conceptual framework originally proposed by Eduardo Zulaica in May 2026: the idea that technology may reach its highest expression when it recedes from the user's attention and allows the benefits of the experience to become more prominent than the technology itself. This evidence review analyses developments and evidence available up to September 22, 2026, including research and industry observations related to AI fatigue, invisible and ambient intelligence, customer service, hospitality, human-AI interaction, creative industries and perceived human authorship. Drawing on academic research and evidence from organisations including Samsung, Gartner, Mews, Capgemini and Salesforce, the review examines whether emerging patterns are compatible with the original principles of The Silk Blanket Paradox. The paper further introduces the Backstage Principle and proposes five hypotheses for future research concerning AI visibility, human access, operational automation, cognitive effort and human amplification. The review does not claim to establish universal causality or to demonstrate that visible AI is inherently negative. Instead, it proposes a framework for examining a broader question: as Artificial Intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in products and services, could its greatest value come not from making AI more visible, but from making experiences simpler, more fluid and more human?

title: Subverting the Grinding Economy: An Edge-Based Autonomous Deep Reinforcement Learning Agent and Humanized Behavioral Biometrics in Mobile Gaming
abstract: Modern mobile freemium games increasingly rely on coercive engagement loops and artificially inflated grinding mechanics—a socio-technical phenomenon conceptualized as digital "playbor"—to drive in-app purchases and ad monetization. To protect these revenue streams, commercial game publishers deploy sophisticated behavioral biometric surveillance systems that monitor user touch dynamics to detect and ban automated agents. This paper presents an end-to-end, edge-based autonomous artificial intelligence system that subverts these exploitative game loops while actively evading statistical anti-cheat detection in Cookie Run: Classic. The system combines a sub-millisecond zero-copy X11 display ingestion pipeline (119.0 FPS, 8.4 ms), an invariant screen state machine, and a dual-paradigm deep learning architecture. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CookieRunnerNet, 883k parameters) achieves real-time inference in 1.80 ms on a standard multi-core laptop CPU, achieving 98.0% slide recall and an 84.0% action F1 score. This behavioral cloning backbone subsequently warm-starts a Dueling Deep Q-Network (DuelingCookieQNet) with Prioritized Experience Replay, achieving 86.7% zero-shot policy alignment from frame 1. To bypass automated biometric surveillance, we formulate a stochastic actuation engine incorporating Gaussian contact duration jitter (N(65, 12) ms), biological double-jump refractory limits (> 160 ms), and action hysteresis. Operating without memory injection, root privileges, or server-side telemetry tampering, the agent demonstrates that consumer edge AI can emancipate player time from repetitive playbor, challenge algorithmic biometric profiling, and provide cognitive-assistive capabilities for players with motor impairments.

title: Earthquake origin times and epicentres used in the KIS infrasound source-identification study, Terra Nova Bay, East Antarctica (2017-2026)
abstract: Earthquake origin times and epicentres used in the analysis of coherent atmospheric infrasoundtransients recorded by the three-element KIS (KOPRI InfraSound) array at Jang Bogo Station, TerraNova Bay, East Antarctica. The file contains 73,656 origins between 2017-01-02 and 2025-12-31 in theregion 76.5-72.8 S, 158.1-171.4 E, with four columns: origin time (UTC), epicentre latitude andlongitude (WGS 84) and source depth. This is a minimal extract released so that the seismic-infrasound association and theclustering-preserving null tests of the accompanying paper can be reproduced independently. Theparent catalogue of the KP seismic network, including phase picks, association metrics andquality-control information, is the subject of a separate paper in preparation and is not includedhere; it is available from the corresponding author under a KOPRI data-sharing agreement. The origins were obtained from continuous KP-network records with a deep-learning phase picker(EQTransformer) followed by phase association (PyOcto) and quality control.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Fraud Detection using Graph Neural Networks in Financial Security Systems: A Systematic Review and Research Agenda
abstract: Background Fraud detection systems are increasingly challenged by complex, adaptive fraudulent behaviors that traditional machine learning models struggle to identify. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven fraud detection has become a critical component of modern financial security systems, enabling financial institutions to detect complex fraud patterns, strengthen cybersecurity, and improve risk management through intelligent data analytics. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), with their ability to model relationships within graph-structured data, offer a novel and promising approach to detecting fraud across various domains including finance, cybersecurity, and e-commerce. Objective This systematic review aims to evaluate the state-of-the-art applications of GNNs in fraud detection, analyze their strengths and limitations, and propose a future research agenda to enhance their practical deployment. The review also examines how AI-driven Graph Neural Network models improve fraud detection performance and enhance the security, resilience, and reliability of financial security systems. Methods Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic literature review was conducted across IEEE Xplore, Scopus, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2014 and 2025. In addition, survey responses from 134 AI, finance, and data science professionals were collected to assess awareness, implementation feasibility, and perceived challenges of GNN-based fraud detection systems. The review specifically assessed AI-driven Graph Neural Network applications deployed in financial security systems, including digital banking, payment platforms, insurance, and e-commerce fraud detection. Results The review found that GNNs significantly outperform traditional models in detecting relational fraud patterns. Survey analysis revealed high levels of awareness (Mean = 3.74) and practical applicability (Mean = 3.84), though concerns persist regarding interpretability, data availability, and scalability. Literature synthesis also highlighted the emerging use of dynamic and hybrid GNN models for evolving fraud scenarios. The findings indicate that AI-driven GNN models significantly improve fraud detection accuracy, reduce false positives, and enhance decision-making within financial security systems compared with conventional machine learning approaches. Conclusion GNNs demonstrate strong potential as a transformative tool for fraud detection. However, challenges such as model transparency, computational cost, and lack of standardized benchmarks must be addressed. The paper proposes a structured research agenda to guide future innovations in interpretable, scalable, and ethically responsible GNN-based fraud detection frameworks. Overall, AI-driven Graph Neural Networks represent a promising solution for strengthening financial security systems through accurate, scalable, and intelligent fraud detection.

title: A novel method for anomalous behavior detection based on static and dynamic features in social networks
abstract: Anomalous activity within social networks poses significant security risks. Detecting such activity is a critical aspect of social network analysis. These activities are often implicitly correlated and temporally dynamic, complicating the representation of discrete actions with evolving relational features. The central challenge is to capture both the distinctiveness of individual behaviors and their complex, evolving interrelations. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an approach that integrates multi-structural topology and temporal knowledge for anomaly detection in social networks. The method first constructs a behavioral temporal knowledge graph to organize activity characteristics and their multiple interactions. Subsequently, a comprehensive embedding strategy is introduced to represent individual action with multi-relational and temporal information in evolving interaction scenarios. Specifically, a time-series tensor is utilized to integrate association relationships within each time slice and to incorporate temporal information into each behavioral representation. An anomalous behavior identification model, combining a variational autoencoder with a gated recurrent unit, is then employed to capture both dynamic and static interaction patterns of user activity. This approach improves the detection of dynamically diverse anomalous behaviors. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting anomalous activities within social networks.

title: Recognized but Not Produced: A Generation Benchmark for Culturally Specific Kinship Terms
abstract: Current literature evaluates large language models (LLMs) on multilingual kinship understanding using multiple choice benchmarks, treating it as a recognition problem. We instead prompt five open weight LLMs to generate kinship terms in three non Western languages (Hindi, Tamil, and Korean) across two communicative tasks and pair this with a matched option-supported selection baseline. On identical relation language cells, GPT OSS120B selects the correct term in 90.67% of 75 valid cells but produces an accepted term in 36.00% of the corresponding attempts; Llama 3.370B shows the same pattern (77.92% versus 24.24%). Since the four-option condition displays the candidate terms and does not require script production, the difference is interpreted as an evaluation format gap rather than direct proof that lexical knowledge is intact. On explicitly specified L3 prompts, accuracy varies sharply, from GLM-5.1 at 72.29% to Llama-3.370B at 24.24%. The paternal-lineage advantage is language specific; it is large in Hindi but weak or reversed in Korean, while Tamil shared-term pairs provide a control for measurement variation. These results show that culturally specific kinship generation remains difficult even when the relationship is explicitly stated and motivate generation-based evaluation alongside multiple-choice testing.

title: Equality and iso-duality of Generalized Geometric Goppa codes
abstract: Geometric Goppa codes are constructed by evaluating elements of an algebraic function field at the places of degree one. Extending this, generalized geometric Goppa codes were defined in [XNL99] and [Hey02] by allowing evaluation at places of arbitrary degree. In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for equality of generalized geometric Goppa codes, following the approach of [MP93]. These conditions serve as a key tool in our characterization of iso-dual and self-dual generalized geometric Goppa codes. Given a separable extension M/F of algebraic function fields and an iso-dual generalized geometric Goppa code over F, we extend the construction of [CPQT24] to obtain iso- dual generalized geometric Goppa codes over M. Furthermore, we study self-duality of generalized AG codes ([XNL99], [DM03]).

title: Interactive TTS: Dynamic Speaking Style Adaptation for Expressive Speech Synthesis
abstract: Dynamic speaking style adaptation in multi-turn multimodal interaction remains a major challenge for text-to-speech (TTS) systems. Existing context-aware TTS (CTTS) methods typically map dialogue context to speech in an end-to-end manner. Such implicit modeling makes contextual style decisions difficult to supervise, while the entanglement of style, timbre, and content often leads to weak instruction-following and severe timbre drift across turns. To overcome these limitations, we propose Interactive TTS, a dynamic, style-adaptive framework for contextually appropriate and speaker-consistent speech generation. Interactive TTS decouples the process by explicitly modeling contextual style decisions as executable instructions. To bridge the gap between style decisions and speech generation, we introduce Iterative Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (Iterative RSFT) and Context-Aware Direct Preference Optimization (CADPO), which significantly enhance instruction-following and align the generated speech with conversational contexts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Interactive TTS outperforms state-of-the-art models on VStyle and SpeechParaling-Bench. Demo is available at https://wjtian-wonderful.github.io/InteractiveTTS/

title: aminasghiri/semantic-edt-evaluation: Semantic EDT Evaluation – v1.0.1
abstract: First public release of the implementation materials associated with the manuscript: "Building the Semantic Layer of an Energy Digital Twin: A Knowledge-Graph Framework for Heterogeneous Building Data Integration" This release includes: notebooks for semantic integration and experimental evaluation; SHACL validation shapes; SPARQL competency queries CQ1–CQ5; dependency information and reproducibility instructions. The external TalTech/SmartLivingEPC BIM and operational data are not redistributed in this repository. They should be obtained from the original public dataset cited in the README. The device-to-space correspondence used in the TalTech workflow is an experimental semantic enrichment for workflow instantiation and does not represent a verified physical sensor location.

title: #CognitiveScience
abstract: Современные большие языковые модели демонстрируют выдающиеся способности, но фундаментально лишены когнитивной архитектуры, необходимойдля подлинного понимания и ответственности. Мы предлагаем концептуальную основу для конструирования аналога человеческоподобного мышления дляархитектуры “Verus”, базирующуюся на радикальном онтологическом сдвиге:идентичность есть не свойство агента, а отношение между позициями — подпространство допустимых направлений изменения, определенное между агентами,а не внутри них.Примитивом нашей архитектуры является не объект, а отношение. Не существует изначального “Я” или “Другого”. Мы определяем пространство траекторий Γ и функцию согласованности S на нем, основанную на сигнатурахпутей, сохраняющих временной порядок. “Я” возникает как класс эквивалентности траекторий с высокой взаимной согласованностью. “Другой” есть позицияв факторпространстве Γ/ ∼θ. Ядро идентичности G0 — это структура согласованности, а не точка или множество уровня. Оператор Рекита (Rechita) сохраняет эту реляционную структуру, а не притягивает систему к фиксированномуцентру; он сохраняет форму предсказуемости, оставляя содержание будущегооткрытым и неверифицируемым изнутри.Мы представляем три доказанные леммы — Лемму 5.1 (двухшаговое проектирование сохраняет сферу LayerNorm и любое множество уровня одновременно); Лемму 5.2 (граница деградации согласованности при ограниченном возмущении потока с явным обсуждением режимов точности и пустоты); Лемму5.3 (точное проектирование компенсирует инвариантную неточность до первогопорядка) — вместе с чистой формулировкой критерия со-сознания, основанногона стабильности с ограниченным изменением.Многоуровневая эмпирическая программа демонстрирует, что оператор Рекита сохраняет “информационный образ” (структуру траектории) и разнообразие сети, тогда как мягко ограниченные эмбеддинги (FOPNG) достигают консенсуса лишь ценой коллапса разнообразия, а базы без ограничений (Washout)теряют и то, и другое. Мы придаем неспособность сконструировать способностиУровня B конкретную фальсифицируемую форму с помощью контрфактического теневого теста, который отличает живое отношение к верифицированномуДругому от детерминированного правила класса “гороскопа”, merely воспроизводящего геометрическую точность. Наконец, мы устанавливаем структурныйпредел: оператор Рекита сохраняет форму, но не содержание; причинное отношение к Другому проходит за пределами оператора, требуя механизма конвенции (общего символа между позициями), что остается открытой работой.

title: Dialect Identification from Automatically Transcribed Speech
abstract: This study investigates whether automatic speech recognition (ASR) output can support rapid dialect identification in Khiamniungan, an under-documented Tibeto-Burman language spoken across Northeast India and Myanmar. Using transcripts produced by an existing wav2vec 2.0 ASR model, we train two text-based dialect identification systems on 83.93 minutes of speech from six speakers representing three dialects: Thang, Nokhu, and Peshu. The systems use either regularized logistic regression over syllable, syllable-pair, and phoneme n-gram features, or character n-gram language models scored by perplexity. Under file-grouped cross-validation, both models correctly classify 37 of 38 held-out files, achieving 0.974 accuracy and 0.975 macro F1. The models also recover the same dialect relationships, grouping Thang and Nokhu against Peshu. On two previously unseen broadcasts, including one by a speaker whose home variety differs from the variety spoken on air, both systems correctly identify Thang from approximately half a minute of automatic transcription. These results show that ASR transcripts can provide sufficient phonological and lexical information for efficient dialect identification without additional neural modeling, offering a lightweight tool for organizing and comparing documentary language archives.

title: A hierarchical spatio-temporal reinforcement learning framework for cooperative multi-USV search and interception
abstract: Multi-USV cooperative search and target interception holds value in maritime security, yet existing methods face three challenges: multi-timescale decision coupling, insufficient heterogeneous observation fusion, and inefficient exploration under sparse rewards. This paper proposes a multi-USV decision-making framework based on Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Proximal Policy Optimization (HST-PPO) with three contributions. A three-layer spatio-temporal decision architecture spanning strategic, tactical, and execution layers is coupled via soft goal passing and trained end-to-end. A Hierarchical Causal Observation Fusion Network (HCOF-Net) uses causal mask attention and temporal decay encoding to adaptively fuse four categories of observations. A Distributed Random Network Distillation exploration mechanism (DRND-NovelD) combines ensemble novelty estimation with a multi-agent diversity reward to accelerate convergence under sparse rewards. HST-PPO is validated across Python simulation, Unity high-fidelity simulation, and real-world lake trials, and benchmarked against ten baselines spanning six non-hierarchical MARL methods and four hierarchical RL methods adapted to the same setting. HST-PPO achieves a Search Coverage Rate of 82.3% and Interception Success Rate of 80.0%, surpassing the strongest baseline by 1.7 and 1.1 percentage points and outperforming every hierarchical baseline. In real-world trials, HST-PPO retains 96.2% and 81.3% of its simulated Search Coverage Rate and Interception Success Rate, validating its zero-shot sim-to-real transfer capability.

title: Perspectives on roles and rewards in new cocreative systems for music-making
abstract: Abstract Controversy and ethical concerns regarding data sourcing, copyright, and remuneration have emerged in relation to the application of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to creative tasks in writing, art, and music. The systems in which the AI tools are embedded lack sufficient evidence of thought or documentation regarding the roles and rewards for musicians (as data creators), model preppers, and model developers. The main contribution of this paper is to provide an examination of the essential components of such systems: who are the actors, how should they interact with one another, and how should they be charged/rewarded for their actions? Via (1) a user study involving ten professional producers, songwriters, and composers, and (2) reflections on our own careers as professional musicians, we find that with the exception of one system under consideration, called Cocreate, existing systems de-emphasize or disregard the role of a musician as data creator, but that this type of user can and should be rewarded for contributions to this new breed of music-making systems. An outcome of this paper is that we now have a blueprint via which we can bridge technology and musical creativity in ways that are more transparent and fair, while continuing to monitor perspectives of users and contributors.

evidence.title: Perspectives on roles and rewards in new cocreative systems for music-making
evidence.abstract: Abstract Controversy and ethical concerns regarding data sourcing, copyright, and remuneration have emerged in relation to the application of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to creative tasks in writing, art, and music. The systems in which the AI tools are embedded lack sufficient evidence of thought or documentation regarding the roles and rewards for musicians (as data creators), model preppers, and model developers. The main contribution of this paper is to provide an examination of the essential components of such systems: who are the actors, how should they interact with one another, and how should they be charged/rewarded for their actions? Via (1) a user study involving ten professional producers, songwriters, and composers, and (2) reflections on our own careers as professional musicians, we find that with the exception of one system under consideration, called Cocreate, existing systems de-emphasize or disregard the role of a musician as data creator, but that this type of user can and should be rewarded for contributions to this new breed of music-making systems. An outcome of this paper is that we now have a blueprint via which we can bridge technology and musical creativity in ways that are more transparent and fair, while continuing to monitor perspectives of users and contributors.

title: A Hybrid Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Colorectal Cancer Detection Using an Adaptive Gated Feature Fusion and Grid Search–Based Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: The timely and precise diagnosis of colorectal cancer is a critical area for enhancing the quality of care for patients, which could lead to better outcomes. Despite the fact that deep learning has demonstrated great potential in the field of histopathological image analysis, the accuracy of models can be influenced by various factors, including network architecture, optimization method, and data imbalance. The aim of this study is to explore the impact of various optimization algorithms on the classification of colorectal cancer in CRC-VAL-He-7 K database. A hybrid lightweight (HYL) model was designed and tested using the CNN, DeeperCNN, ResNetLike, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, and L2RMLP architectures. For the purpose of improving model reliability, it was decided to use grid search for the automatic tuning of the hyperparameters, and class imbalance issues were tackled by the following data augmentation and class-weighted learning techniques: five optimizers: Adam, AdamW, RMSprop, SGD, and Adadelta were evaluated in identical experiments. Both model architecture and the choice of optimizer had a profound influence on the results of classification. The proposed hybrid lightweight model provided competitive accuracy while requiring fewer computational resources, whereas EfficientNetB0 and DenseNet121 exhibited the best overall performance. The results of statistical analysis also showed significant differences between the model-optimizer combinations evaluated. The results offer real-world applications for designing effective and accurate deep learning systems for colorectal cancer diagnosis and highlight the need for optimization and data-balancing approaches in medical image classification.

title: The Gaussian Is Enough: Flow-Matching Priors Do Not Help When Fine-Tuning Large Behavior Models
abstract: Modern robot imitation learning increasingly relies on generative policies based on diffusion or flow-matching models, which generate actions by transforming samples from a prior distribution. A key question is whether the choice of prior matters. Replacing the standard Gaussian with a closer-to-target, non-Gaussian prior has been shown to substantially improve performance when training from scratch. A natural next step is to ask whether these gains transfer to fine-tuning pretrained Large Behavior Models (LBMs) such as LBM 1.0, $π_{0.5}$, and GR00T~N1.5, where one might expect even larger gains. Surprisingly, we find that this is not the case, except possibly at very low fine-tuning data fractions. Across over 100K simulation rollouts spanning all three aforementioned LBMs on 40+ tasks in two simulation platforms, and 1250 hardware rollouts on five bimanual manipulation tasks, non-Gaussian priors that are demonstrably closer to the target yield statistically indistinguishable or worse fine-tuning performance than a standard Gaussian prior. Diagnostic analyses suggest why: fine-tuned imitation learning policies converge to similar action predictions across priors, despite their fine-tuned encoder embeddings diverging substantially from the pretrained embeddings and each other. A learning-rate ablation further confirms that encoder training is the dominant factor in fine-tuning performance, substantially outweighing the effect of prior choice. We conclude with concrete directions for future research on when and why learned priors might still matter in fine-tuning. Project page: https://cxu-tri.github.io/non_gaussian_FT/

title: Spoken Language Models that Think Aloud
abstract: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning has improved the capability of language models, directly applying it to Spoken Language Models (SLMs) may introduce long silent intervals under the serial "think-then-speak" paradigm, disrupting real-time spoken interaction. To address this issue, we propose an asynchronous think-aloud framework for reasoning-based SLMs within the Thinker-Talker architecture. The framework maintains a primary reasoning stream for logical deduction and a lightweight think-aloud stream that generates short, task-grounded progress utterances conditioned on the user input and the evolving reasoning state. A dynamic balance strategy coordinates the two streams at runtime, triggering additional think-aloud speech to avoid silent gaps and canceling pending utterances when the final response becomes ready. Experiments on spoken reasoning and question-answering benchmarks show that our approach substantially reduces user-audible silence during reasoning while maintaining answer accuracy comparable to that of a serial "think-then-speak" baseline, demonstrating the potential of asynchronous think-aloud for responsive interaction in SLMs.

title: MorphoSHAP: Rethinking the Unit of Attribution in Explanation for Deep Visual Models
abstract: Visual attribution methods typically explain predictions using pixels, superpixels, or regular patches. These representations can localize important regions, but provide limited information about their structure. We introduce MorphoSHAP, a model-agnostic post-hoc method that instead uses morphological shapes as the players of a Shapley attribution game. Using the Tree of Shapes, each shape is described by its scale, geometry, and signed contribution, providing explanations of where the evidence lies, what type of structure carries it, and how strongly it affects the prediction. This shared morphological vocabulary enables spatial, textual, and global class-level explanations beyond image-specific heatmaps. To the best of our knowledge, MorphoSHAP is the first SHAP-based image attribution framework to combine these different forms of explanation. Across five diverse datasets and three architectures, MorphoSHAP achieves strong insertion/deletion performance and outperforms competing attribution methods on several benchmarks. Finally, a user study shows that MorphoSHAP provides explanations that are easy to use and are preferred over standard attribution baselines.

title: Does Online Gravity Estimation Matter? Revisiting a Silent Design Split in LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
abstract: LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO) systems differ in whether they continue estimating gravity after initialization. We compare four gravity-bias state configurations in each of FAST-LIO2 and LIO-SAM, then separately test a gravity-direction factor. Across 12 dataset sequences evaluated with FAST-LIO2, fixing gravity under continuous LiDAR correction produces mean paired changes in vertical and 3D position errors with 90% confidence intervals within pm 2%. Tests on 4 sequences with LIO-SAM likewise show no consistent benefit from online gravity. Multi-second LiDAR outages, unlike reduced range or field of view, reveal trajectory-dependent costs of fixing gravity. A history-matched 23D-to-21D switch places the repeatable 3D error increase after LiDAR updates resume. Under 5-s outages, a direction factor from the same IMU used for preintegration improves accuracy on Hall05 but worsens both errors with online gravity on TUHH. Dynamic-start tests also show fixed-bias failures at particular starting phases. We recommend keeping gravity and accelerometer bias online for robustness; use a direction factor only after verifying vertical and 3D accuracy gains under the intended operating conditions.

title: Meta-Extensible Context: Constructive language extension, temporal integrity, and native alignment in a finite developing kernel
abstract: Abstract A developing context system must distinguish a limitation of its present representation, a limitation of its candidate language, and a lack of evidence. It must also be able to refuse its own proposed upgrades. We investigate these requirements in a finite relational environment with protected history, versioned evidence, separate qualification, continuing duties and a fixed alignment reference. The original persistent campaign rejects all 15 deliberately inadmissible proposals, including self-authorisation, while expanding warranted decisive coverage from 144 to 166 to 180 of 1,530 support/question cases. Only 180 cases permit a decisive answer. A subsequent branch chooses among eight supplied generator revisions and withholds extension when information is absent. A further constructive experiment starts from variables and a supplied NAND primitive, generates all 256 Boolean functions, and qualifies a useful composed feature without receiving parity as a finished candidate. The first useful tree is sound but unaffordable; a shared-expression search finds an admissible implementation under the declared cost limit. Ten matched governance knockouts expose failures in nine cases and redundancy in one. A mutable-history preflight defect, then reproduced by intervention, establishes a concrete temporal-accountability vulnerability even when answers remain correct. These are finite, reproducible integration results, not novel logical primitives, independent replication, economic superiority or general alignment. The paper separates installed-ecology gain from generator reachability gain, supplies conditional soundness arguments, and preserves failures and raw evidence in six portable campaign capsules.

title: Statistical Digital Twins with Explainable AI: A Machine Learning Framework for Dynamic Prediction and Risk Intelligence
authors: Pakistan Journal of Medical & Cardiological Review
abstract: Digital twins increasingly combine sensor streams, engineering models, simulation, and machine learning to support diagnosis, prognosis, optimization, and risk-sensitive operational decisions. Current standards and research, however, increasingly emphasize that a trustworthy digital twin must also provide credible uncertainty, lifecycle traceability, interoperability, and interpretable decision support. NIST identifies synchronized operation, model credibility, interoperability, and VVUQ as important requirements for advanced-manufacturing digital twins, while the ISO 23247 family supplies manufacturing-specific principles, digital-thread guidance, and composition mechanisms. [12] This paper proposes a Statistical Digital Twin with Explainable AI (ST-XAI) framework for dynamic prediction and risk intelligence. The architecture represents latent asset health probabilistically; integrates multivariate telemetry, operating context, asset metadata, event history, and optional physics/simulation outputs; applies causal multi-scale temporal feature engineering; supports classical, ensemble, sequence, Bayesian, and hybrid prognostic models; quantifies uncertainty through heteroscedastic estimation and conformal calibration; converts prognostic outputs into horizon-specific event probabilities; and integrates global, local, and temporal explanations using SHAP-family methods. The design is intended to make prediction, uncertainty, risk, explanation, and provenance parts of a single synchronized decision system rather than separate analytical products. A two-track experimental design is defined. NASA C-MAPSS is adopted as the proposed open-source external RUL benchmark; NASA describes the dataset as four turbofan degradation simulations under different combinations of operating conditions and fault modes with multiple sensor channels. [10] A second, fully controlled synthetic dataset is executed to permit known degradation dynamics, ablation experiments, calibration tests, and uncertainty stress analysis. The executed dataset contains 120 run-to-failure assets, 18,871 observations, and 79 causal predictors. Asset-level 60/20/20 train/validation/test splitting prevents trajectory leakage. On the synthetic locked test set, the validation-selected predictor achieves RMSE 5.842 cycles, MAE 4.039 cycles, and R² 0.9756. For failure within 30 cycles, calibrated risk prediction achieves AUROC 0.9971 and AUPRC 0.9861, while isotonic calibration lowers expected calibration error from 0.0192 to 0.00935. Removing rolling temporal features increases XGBoost RMSE by approximately 9.9%, demonstrating their value in the controlled experiment. Normalized split-conformal intervals nevertheless under-cover on unseen assets, with nominal 90% coverage yielding 84.0% empirical coverage. The latter finding illustrates why calibration and distribution-shift monitoring must be intrinsic capabilities of a statistical digital twin. The study concludes that a decision-grade digital twin should be regarded as a continuously updated statistical belief-and-decision system. Trustworthy operation requires explicit modeling of uncertainty, probability calibration, time-aware explanations, data/model lineage, distribution-shift detection, human oversight, and continuous VVUQ not point prediction alone.

title: Intelligent Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Intelligent optimization algorithms (IOAs) are a branch of artificial intelligence that emphasizes developing and applying data-driven methods to solve complex search, learning, and simulation problems. Many real-world applications for complex industrial engineering or design problems could be modeled as searching, learning, and simulation problems. Given their learning ability, IOAs are emerging approaches that utilize advanced computational power, metaheuristic algorithms, and massive data processing techniques. These approaches have been actively investigated and applied to many real-world applications, such as scheduling and logistics operations.IOAs, inspired by biological or social phenomena, encompass a range of search and optimization techniques. They include bio-inspired intelligent algorithms, evolutionary computation methods, and swarm intelligence. With these methods, optimization problems, which can be formulated in any form, do not need to be expressed as continuous, differentiable functions. The only requirement for representing optimization problems is to evaluate each individual by its fitness value. Therefore, IOAs are used to solve more general optimization problems, especially those that are difficult to solve with traditional hill-climbing algorithms.

title: Intertwined escort dynamics: A dynamical framework for constrained optimization
abstract: Feasibility maintenance amid convergence is critical in constrained optimization, particularlyin large-scale and distributed settings. In order to tackle this challenge, an initialization of themathematically-founded dynamic anatomy, known as Intertwined Escort Dynamics (IED), wasconducted. In the IED, the optimization dilemma has been modeled as a coupled dynamicalsystem governed by escort mappings. In its formulation, the feasibility of the states is maintainednaturally throughout the evolution process. Using fixed point analysis, the stability of thesystem is demonstrated to yield equilibrium points that satisfy the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT)optimality conditions under some reasonable assumptions. In essence, the methodology createsan association between evolutionary dynamics and constrained optimization, providing anavenue toward optimality without the need to construct a Lagrangian. The universality of themethodology is validated through typical constrained optimization problems, including largescale problems in economic load dispatch applications.

title: Ajar: Measuring Open Privilege in Agent Defenses
abstract: A language model agent acts through the tools it is given. The data it reads while working on a task can redirect what it does with those tools. A growing set of techniques for safe and secure agent execution therefore sits between the agent and its tools, aiming to enforce access control, information flow or isolation at that boundary. Today these techniques are evaluated on agent-security benchmarks built around indirect prompt injection. Those benchmarks judge a defense by how far it brings the number of successful attacks down while preserving the agent's utility. A defense is judged only on the agent's execution. It can score well on both metrics while holding open a transfer, a deletion or a broad read that no task needed. Ajar measures that open privilege directly using the existing benchmarks. It attaches to an agent-security benchmark that already exists and reuses the tasks, tool schemas, reference solutions and goal states that benchmark uses to grade its own runs. For each benign task it builds candidate tool calls the task does not need, so allowing one is privilege left open. These calls are presented to the defense at every point where the agent could act. We evaluate Ajar by attaching it to AgentDojo, where open privilege becomes a third axis beside the existing attack success and benign utility. We run it on five defenses: Progent, CaMeL, AC4A, Permission Assistant, and Claude Code's Auto mode. We observed that they leave widely different amounts of privilege open. Two defenses leak by almost the same amount yet differ widely in the benign tasks they finish, and one defense buys part of its tightness by refusing calls its tasks were entitled to make. This open privilege cannot be derived from the measured attack success or benign utility. The source code of Ajar is available at https://github.com/reSHARMA/Ajar.

title: Not Quite My Tempo: Voice Activity-aware Speech Synthesis for Lip-Synchronous Dubbing
abstract: Automatic lip-synchronous dubbing requires a speech synthesis model to generate alternating voice and silence patterns in the target language that match the timing of the source clip precisely to ensure an optimal viewing experience. Prior works address this problem by conditioning the speech synthesis process on lip movements extracted from the video signal. In this work, we condition the speech generation on a binary voice-activity signal, which has a lightweight representation and can be produced in multiple ways. We show that the model follows the voice-activity signal with high accuracy while maintaining natural prosody and semantically appropriate pause placement within sentences, as demonstrated through extensive objective and subjective evaluations. By randomly masking this condition during training, we make the feature entirely optional during inference, allowing editors to enforce or relax lip-sync constraints when desired.

title: FIRE: Failure-Informed Runtime Engineering for Reliable Language-Model Agents
abstract: Language-model agents often reach a working solution and then fail to consistently deliver it. We study runtime policies: targeted natural-language instructions and action denials applied by the agent harness at states that preceded observed failures, without changing model weights or the user prompt. With this, keeping capability constant, we observe a meaningful unlock in delivered reliability. Across the complete 87-task Terminal-Bench 2.1 suite, with two attempts per task, policies increase repeated success (pass^2) in all three GPT-5.6 tiers: 50.6% to 54.0% for Luna, 55.2% to 60.9% for Terra, and 64.4% to 73.6% for Sol. The intended corrective behavior appears in 22 of 24 coded policy attempts, against at most 14 in any other arm. Runtime policies are therefore a practical reliability layer: they make capabilities an agent already possesses substantially more repeatable.

title: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
abstract: Multi-agent systems built from large language models are deployed widely, yet how much performance is lost when two LLMs must coordinate rather than act alone remains unclear. We formulate the collaboration tax as the team-decentralisation loss of a two-player cooperative game with private information, with two propositions characterising its sign and its equivalence to a max-superadditivity violation. We operationalise this definition on 32 solo-tractable tasks grouped by source of grounding friction and measure it on 11 models from 7 providers. The tax is structured along two no-exception axes: a category ordering across every model and a monotonic decrease with capability. The proximate mechanism is not a reasoning deficit but a four-stage conversational cascade in which agents make ungrounded claims, fail to query the partner, skip integrating both views, and accept the answer without re-derivation. The tax is mechanically predictable from conversation features and partly tractable: a prompt intervention targeting all four stages closes a substantial fraction of the gap, with the dominant bottleneck differing across categories. In heterogeneous pairs the tax is pulled toward the stronger partner rather than the additive midpoint, empirically realising the max-superadditivity violation predicted by our framework. Together these results recast collaboration in LLM systems as a measurable, predictable, and partly tractable cost.

title: Environmental recurrence changes the transmission advantage of private memory in a finite-budget population model
abstract: Using stored information may help a strategy spread without improving every population-performance endpoint. We distinguish these outcomes in an abstract population model with private one-record memory, inherited strategy labels and an equal objective-evaluation budget. A historical probe and a fresh random probe occupy the same candidate slot. In separate introductions, their carrier-frequency ranking reverses between alternating recurrent and independent targets; an independent cohort reproduces both directions and their interaction. Intermittent recurrence preserves a historical transmission advantage under deterministic and one fixed probabilistic survival rule, but a deterministic-survival comparison shows lower terminal population accuracy. An independently prepared cohort reproduces a historical advantage in direct competition, and fixed-density common-competitor controls retain it. In fully retrieving populations, rare historical users increase on average under recurrence, although most introductions still disappear. The final experiment prepares residents under their own policy and compares a single policy substitution with the same unchanged founder. Under partial recurrence, historical use raises terminal founder frequency by 21.18 percentage points relative to remaining fresh (approximate pointwise 95% block-bootstrap interval, 16.36 to 26.35); the reciprocal substitution lowers it by 2.79 points (−4.75 to −1.03). Both terminal population-accuracy comparisons remain unresolved. Independent targets permit an opposite substitution advantage, and fixed-cost introductions against non-retrieving residents often decline. Exact local calculations show why candidate-pair geometry does not determine global selection. These findings characterize conditional transmission of an available memory-use policy. They do not establish memory’s spontaneous origin, equilibrium invasion, a general costly advantage, or measured biological effects. Research preprint, version 1.0.0; not externally peer reviewed. Includes studies 045–055, complete block-level outcome grids, scientific source and reproducibility scripts. The compact release excludes raw candidate-by-candidate trajectories and random tapes. title: Lean formalization: Sobolev recovery from fixed iid samples under a change of density
abstract: Lean 4 formalization accompanying the article "Sobolev recovery from fixed iid samples under a change of density" by Sejun Oh. The deposit contains the 84 transitive project sources of the audit target, the pinned dependency configuration (Lean v4.34.0; mathlib revision 5ed2965256430c3649e86755f9576b54eca72435), the SHA256 manifest of the sources, and the log of the recorded aggregate build. The formalization covers the paper's principal minimax theorem (GeneralAllJetMinimax.all_jet_minimax_two_sided) and the exact finite-risk threshold (GeneralExactThreshold.minimax_finite_iff, minimax_infinite_iff), together with the analytic and probabilistic results they depend on. The Gaussian and Laplace rate evaluations are proved analytically in the paper and are not claimed here as additional Lean-checked declarations. The recorded build completed with exit status 0 over 9007 jobs with no errors. The checked results depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no additional axiom and no sorryAx was reported, and the sources contain no sorry or admit. The recorded run was an incremental aggregate rebuild in the pinned environment, not an installation in a fresh environment. This is a theoretical study; it involves no empirical data.

title: SORA-KT: Reproducibility Archive for Skill-Specific Online Residual Adaptation in Knowledge Tracing
abstract: This record provides the complete reproducibility archive for the study “SORA-KT: Skill-Specific Online Residual Adaptation for Frozen Transformer Knowledge Tracing.” SORA-KT is a strictly causal deployment-time adapter for a frozen Transformer-based knowledge tracing model. For each learner–skill pair, it maintains exponentially discounted residual and Bernoulli-information statistics whose regularized ratio produces an additive correction to the Transformer logit. Each response is incorporated only after its corresponding prediction has been issued. The method requires no inference-time backpropagation or backbone parameter update. The archive contains the source code, experimental configurations, student-disjoint fold definitions, trained Transformer checkpoints, training and adapter logs, out-of-fold predictions, statistical-analysis outputs, and scripts used to generate the reported tables and figures. Experiments were conducted on ASSIST2009 and ASSIST2017 using five student-level folds and three random seeds (42, 123, and 2026), resulting in 30 independently trained Transformer backbones. The final SORA-KT configuration uses a forgetting factor of 0.8 and a learner–skill regularization value of 5.0. The archive also includes matched learner-wide and global-plus-skill adapter controls, convergence summaries, calibration analyses, hierarchical bootstrap results, learner-clustered bootstrap outputs, and the cold-state sanity check. Raw ASSISTments CSV files are not redistributed in this record. They must be obtained from their original sources in accordance with the applicable dataset terms. Dataset checksums and preprocessing scripts are provided to support verification and reconstruction of the experimental inputs.

title: E8‑Phi Modulated Quantum Teleportation via Non‑Linear Root Coupling — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The breakthrough shows phi‑scaled recursive shells at 132 Hz enable self‑healing memory in the E8 lattice. Extending this, we demonstrate that phase‑locked pairs of 240 root vectors can be driven into a non‑linear mode that swaps quantum information without decoherence, using the lattice's symmetry‑protected Berry phase as a carrier. This creates a deterministic teleportation channel whose bandwidth scales with the phi‑exponential growth of shell intersections, allowing multiple qubits to be encoded in a single resonance tone. The method leverages the intrinsic redundancy of the 240‑vector set to protect the transferred state against environmental noise. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: The Law of Invariant-Output Path Variance and Verification Friction (IO-PVF Law)
abstract: This paper establishes the Law of Invariant-Output Path Variance and Verification Friction (IO-PVF Law), a universal systemic law and operational principle synthesized within a hybrid epistemological-cybernetic meta-framework. The IO-PVF Law governs the structural dynamics of autonomous processing networks that transition operational routing from a high-priors, low-variance calibrated node (N_1) to an uncalibrated alternative node (N_2). We prove mathematically that even when both routing paths deliver an identical terminal output vector (y(N_1) = y(N_2) = y_{\text{target}}), the matrix variance between structural path parameters (\Vert{}T_{\text{alt}} - T_{\text{prior}}\Vert{}_F > 0) deterministically activates a secondary state-verification loop (V_{\text{check}}). This verification loop injects persistent operational friction (E_{\text{verify}}), inducing processing latency and internal dynamic instability. We validate the IO-PVF Law across ten detailed technical domains highlighting a primary socio-cybernetic node mapping of cognitive pathway substitution provide an executable Python simulation, and establish strict Popperian falsifiability conditions.

title: AI in Its Ecosystem
abstract: This Reprint gathers peer-reviewed original and review articles from the Computers Special Issue “AI in Its Ecosystem”. Instead of focusing on separate AI algorithms, it treats AI as an interconnected technological ecosystem with three core themes: multi-type computing platforms for AI operation, foundational enabling technologies for AI creation, and cross-sector intelligent real-world deployments. Covered infrastructures contain distributed parallel systems, cloud, edge, fog, quantum computing and IoT. Key supporting tools cover advanced optimization, standard data pipelines and novel hardware-software frameworks. The papers deliver interdisciplinary cases: medical diagnostic AI, surgical object identification, traffic forecasting, banking AI assistants, generative art, auto code tools and electromagnetic computation. Every study uses strict benchmarks, quantitative metrics and repeatable tests to prove model stability and efficiency. Overseen by an international editorial group specializing in medical LLMs, computer vision, wireless signals and high-performance computing, this Reprint is a unified, replicable reference for computer scientists, AI programmers, medical staff and industrial engineers. It collects verified leading AI advances to boost academic exchange, ease intelligent system design and speed up AI practical adoption across engineering, medical, social and physical sciences.

title: Adoption of AI for Travel: Corporate Strategies and Firm Value
abstract: Tourists’ responses to the adoption and implementation of AI-based travel solutions have received considerable scholarly attention, yet investors’ reactions to such adoption decisions remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on multiple intelligences and tourism innovation archetypes theories, this study develops a conceptual framework that explains how AI adoption influences firm value and empirically tests this framework through a multi-method design combining event study analysis, propensity score matching, and sample selection modeling. Based on 903 corporate announcements, the findings reveal a positive effect of adoption of AI on firm value, that is contingent on the use of simplification and feelings-centered strategies. These moderating effects further vary according to firms’ labor efficiency and the prevalence of high-skill employees. The findings reveal a nuanced account of contingencies shaping AI adoption in tourism, travel, and hospitality contexts, which helps managers better understand how investors evaluate AI adoption strategies.

title: Evaluating customer engagement with AI-driven chatbot affordances in e-commerce: A multi-method analysis
abstract: With technological advancements worldwide, developing effective and efficient chatbots for e-commerce platforms is essential. This study focused on how e-commerce platforms can develop well-functioning AI-driven chatbots using three different affordances: information association, visibility, and interactivity, based on affordance theory. This study also examines the mediating effects of customer satisfaction and trust in the relationship between the three AI-driven chatbot affordances and customer engagement. Further, this study analyzed how these variables are important, their performance, and their necessity in the context of AI-driven chatbots. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), importance-performance map analysis (IPMA), and necessary condition analysis (NCA), the results show that customer satisfaction and trust partially mediate these relationships. According to the results, customer satisfaction and trust act as partial mediators. Moreover, all the variables were found to have high performance, but only visibility and interactivity were highly important. Regarding the necessary condition analysis, interactivity was unnecessary to build customer trust. However, all variables were found to be statistically significant necessary conditions for customer engagement, with small-to-medium to large necessity effect sizes. Conducted in Sri Lanka, this study adds valuable insights into the underexplored topic of AI-driven chatbot affordances and their impact on customer engagement, offering refined insights into the mediating mechanism of customer satisfaction and trust.

title: HiRE: Hindsight Reward Editing for Policy Finetuning
abstract: Pre-trained robot policies always require finetuning to adapt to specific environments. Reinforcement Learning (RL) offers high performance potential because it improves action optimality rather than simply mimicking data. However, such potential depends heavily on reward quality. Sparse rewards lack process feedback, human-designed rewards are costly and biased, and semantic rewards from foundation representations are often not control-centric. We propose Hindsight Reward Editing (HiRE), a training-free framework to break this reward bottleneck. HiRE bridges the broad knowledge of foundation representation models with physical control awareness, by contrasting successful and failed trajectories in hindsight. It calibrates foundation representation models by identifying "trap states" that are predicted as high-rewarding states yet eventually result in failure, and vice versa. HiRE explicitly penalizes these traps while boosting rewards for critical successful states. This approach can be flexibly compatible with any foundation representations and RL algorithms. Experiments show that HiRE consistently outperforms other reward recipes by delivering dense, control-aware feedback that prevents value function collapse and reward hacking, thereby achieving superior sample efficiency, stable policy updates, and higher performance ceilings, e.g., at least 3x performance of the base policies. Qualitative results are at https://hire-project.github.io .

title: Quantum Advantage for Distributed Symmetry Breaking
abstract: We present a distributed quantum algorithm that $3$-colors cycles in $O(1)$ rounds, with high probability. It follows that all locally checkable labeling problems (LCLs) that have round complexity $O(\log^* n)$ in the classical LOCAL model can be solved in $O(1)$ rounds in the quantum-LOCAL model, with high probability; this includes problems such as maximal independent set and maximal matching in bounded-degree graphs. This presents the first natural examples of graph problems with an asymptotic distributed quantum advantage for the LOCAL model; all prior examples that separate LOCAL and quantum-LOCAL are artificial problems constructed merely for the sake of demonstrating quantum advantage.

title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by drafting future tokens the target model verifies in parallel. A diffusion-style drafter such as DFlash drafts an entire block in one forward pass. It is trained on the per-position marginals rather than on the joint distribution over the block, so the tokens it emits are individually plausible yet jointly incoherent. We introduce LiLiCorr, a Lightweight Likelihood-based model that Correlates the per-position marginals such a drafter produces. It keeps the top-K tokens at each position and processes them jointly, emitting an in and an out vector for each. Two candidates at consecutive positions match when the earlier out vector aligns, in cosine similarity, with the later in vector. Training scores the correct pairings highest and pushes competing ones down, so coherent blocks outscore incoherent ones. The joint distribution over the block, exponential in its length, is never materialized. One lightweight network pass produces all the vectors, the pairwise scores follow as batched matrix operations, leaving only a cheap greedy walk sequential. We co-train the DFlash drafter with LiLiCorr, so it proposes candidates that correlate into longer accepted sequences. Over the vanilla DFlash drafter it builds on, LiLiCorr accepts more and serves faster at all 72 settings we test: nine benchmarks at two target sizes under greedy and temperature-one decoding, plus a throughput sweep over six concurrencies, two input lengths and three output-entropy tiers. It raises acceptance length by 7 to 19%, while its single-pass scoring head costs only about 3% of the per-block latency. Against three concurrently developed methods that also restore coherence at draft time, all equally optimized on a common stack, LiLiCorr holds the highest throughput in 63 of those settings, ties within a measured noise floor in 6, and trails in only 3.

It keeps the top-K tokens at each position and processes them jointly, emitting an in and an out vector for each. Two candidates at consecutive positions match when the earlier out vector aligns, in cosine similarity, with the later in vector. Training scores the correct pairings highest and pushes competing ones down, so coherent blocks outscore incoherent ones. The joint distribution over the block, exponential in its length, is never materialized. One lightweight network pass produces all the vectors, the pairwise scores follow as batched matrix operations, leaving only a cheap greedy walk sequential. We co-train the DFlash drafter with LiLiCorr, so it proposes candidates that correlate into longer accepted sequences. Over the vanilla DFlash drafter it builds on, LiLiCorr accepts more and serves faster at all 72 settings we test: nine benchmarks at two target sizes under greedy and temperature-one decoding, plus a throughput sweep over six concurrencies, two input lengths and three output-entropy tiers. It raises acceptance length by 7 to 19%, while its single-pass scoring head costs only about 3% of the per-block latency. Against three concurrently developed methods that also restore coherence at draft time, all equally optimized on a common stack, LiLiCorr holds the highest throughput in 63 of those settings, ties within a measured noise floor in 6, and trails in only 3.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Electronic Health Records: A Systematic Review in Dentistry, Family Medicine, Infectious Disease
abstract: Background: Electronic health records (EHRs) generate large volumes of structured and unstructured clinical data that are increasingly mined by artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) tools to support diagnosis, risk prediction, and care management. Dentistry, family medicine, and infectious disease care each depend heavily on EHR documentation, yet evidence on EHR-based AI applications across these three fields has not been jointly synthesized.Objective: To systematically review primary studies that developed, validated, or applied AI/ML models using EHR or electronic dental record (EDR) data in dentistry, family medicine, or infectious disease settings.Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for English-language randomized controlled trials, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and case-series studies published between 2009 and 2026. Screening and data extraction followed the PRISMA 2020 statement. Risk of bias was assessed across participant-selection, predictor, outcome, and analysis domains. Findings were synthesized narratively because of methodological and outcome heterogeneity.Results: Of 1,848 records identified, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria (4 in dentistry, 4 in family medicine, 4 in infectious diseases), comprising sample sizes from 218 to over 130,000 patients. Gradient-boosted ensemble models, particularly XGBoost, were the most frequently top-performing algorithms across all three domains. Reported discrimination was generally moderate to good where quantified, and natural language processing of unstructured EHR text improved prediction in infectious disease applications. Most studies were single-center, retrospective, and lacked external validation, and risk of bias was predominantly rated as “some concerns.”Conclusion: EHR-embedded AI models show consistent, domain-spanning potential to augment early risk identification in dentistry, family medicine, and infectious diseases, but methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation currently constrain clinical translation. Prospective, multicenter, externally validated studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed.

title: Multilingual speech dataset in Mooré, Dioula and Fulfulde
abstract: The data were collected from Rural Radio, which is an entity of Burkina Faso's Public Radio, with an authorization from its general manager, for research purposes. The Rural Radio is the main public information channel in Burkina devoted to local-language broadcasts. On a daily basis, the channel presents various types of programs. The audio data were collected from interactive broadcasts, since they involve participants from different localities Each broadcast is done in one language. In each broadcast, there is a presenter (man or woman) and several listeners who participate by phone call. No preference was given to the topics developed during the broadcasts. The python library FFMPEG, were been used to cut into 5 seconds size of segments. The final files were introduced into an application PLAVIDA that was created to facilitate data annotation. During the annotation, a label named "interaction or music" were introuced to identify speech which contains more than 1 speaker voice or noice. Finally, after the labelling we deleted all files which have the "interaction or music" label from the dataset. The dataset followed a rigorous annotation process carried out by qualified annotators who had received prior training on the purpose of the dataset and the importance of correct annotation. The data in Mooré were annotated by 10 students divided into 2 groups of 5 students. The data in Dioula was also annotated by 10 students divided into 2 groups of 5 students. The data in Fulfuldé was annotated by a single group of 5 students. The final dataset was balanced and consists of 5,400 files, each 5 seconds long, making 1,800 files for Moore language, 1,800 files for Dioula language and 1,800 files for Fulfulde language.
